newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's set to make value offer.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's set to make value offer.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. said Wednesday it plans a "value offering" and a franchise official said the special promotion would include 55-cent sandwiches in a bid to boost sales and traffic at its restaurants.
In a statement, McDonald's offered no details but said it "will be good news for our customers and our franchisees and our business ... but bad news for the competition."
A franchise official, meanwhile, said McDonald's was planning a deep-discount promotion to jump-start customer traffic and sales at its restaurants.

Dick Adams, chairman of the Consortium, an independent association of McDonald's franchisees, said the fast-food giant is planning a 12-month promotion that will feature a different sandwich priced at 55 cents each month when the order includes french fries and a drink.
He said McDonald's was expected to present the plan in a satellite broadcast to operators across the country on Thursday.
"They (franchisees) are going to vote for it," Adams said. "They are being told that it's the only plan that is available."
The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that McDonald's plan, including the 55-cent price promotion, will be its biggest discounting programme ever.
The newspaper, quoting an internal company document, said, "McDonald's pricing isn't competitive" and that cutting prices could reverse "the declining momentum of sales, transaction and cash flow."
The newspaper also said McDonald's strategy could "set off a price war of unprecedented proportions."
The stock prices of McDonald's, Wendy's International Inc. and Burger King's parent company all fell, reflecting investors' fears of a fast-food price war.

McDonald's fell $2.50 to $44.75 and Wendy's slid $1.625 to $20.625 on the New York Stock Exchange, where the shares were among the most active in afternoon trading. American shares of Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc, which owns Burger King, fell $1.125 to $30.50, also on the NYSE.
In its statement, McDonald's said, "The wild conclusions reached by The Wall Street Journal today are flat out wrong."

"Conclusions about the state of our business, the price war and the conclusion about how this value-promotion will affect the business of our franchisees are all flat-out wrong," Jack Daly, McDonald's chief spokesman, said.
